title: The Note
text: She crossed out ‘sorry’ at the beginning of the note. The sentence underneath finally had room to stand.
socialCaption: There are apologies that belong in a letter. This one didn’t.

title: The Earrings
text: She wore the bright earrings to buy groceries. The tomatoes were not impressed. She was.
socialCaption: The ordinary Tuesday has never objected to a little ceremony.

title: Changing Her Mind
text: She changed her mind at noon. It wasn’t a betrayal of the woman who woke up that morning.
socialCaption: New information is allowed to change a decision.

title: A Door from Her Side
text: She could want someone badly and still want the door to open from her side.
socialCaption: Desire and choice belong in the same room.

title: The Steady Voice
text: She waited until her voice was steady. The answer had been no long before that.
socialCaption: A boundary doesn’t begin when it becomes easy to say.

title: Asking for Help
text: There is a kind of confidence that looks like asking for help before the whole shelf comes down.
socialCaption: I’d trust that kind of confidence with a set of tools.

title: No One Version
text: She could be tender at breakfast and difficult by four. Both versions knew how to tell the truth.
socialCaption: A full person will occasionally inconvenience the easy description.

title: A Little More Sky
text: She didn’t follow the stars. She stepped outside because she wanted a little more sky.
socialCaption: Wonder doesn’t need to make every decision for us.

title: The Dishes
text: The first stars appeared while the dishes were still wet. That felt about right to me.
socialCaption: The enormous and the ordinary rarely wait for one another.

title: Ancient Light
text: A telescope can show you the past in astonishing detail. It’s less useful for deciding whether to send that text.
socialCaption: I remain impressed by both problems, for different reasons.

title: Kitchen Calendar
text: I keep looking for meaning in constellations. So far the kitchen calendar has been more accurate, but nowhere near as interesting.
socialCaption: A little humility belongs next to wonder.

title: An Unfinished Evening
text: The moon came up over the neighbor’s roof while she was still folding laundry. She watched anyway.
socialCaption: She didn’t have to finish everything before looking up.

title: The First Point
text: Even a perfect circle needs someone to choose where the pencil touches the paper.
socialCaption: A small human decision sits at the beginning of the most exact drawing.

title: No Finished Point
text: There isn’t a single place on a spiral labeled “finished.” I keep drawing them anyway.
socialCaption: Maybe that’s part of why the shape stays interesting.

title: What the Ruler Knows
text: The ruler can tell me the lines are straight. It can’t tell me whether the picture feels right.
socialCaption: Precision is wonderful. I still have to make a choice.

title: Pattern or Prediction
text: There’s a difference between a pattern and a prediction. I’ve mistaken one for the other more than once.
socialCaption: I find that worth remembering whenever a coincidence gets my attention.

title: After the Note
text: I can hear a note stop and still feel it in my chest. Sound doesn’t always leave when it’s finished speaking.
socialCaption: Some sensations linger. Music is very good at demonstrating that.

title: The Fifth Listen
text: The song hadn’t changed. Somewhere between the first listen and the fifth, I had.
socialCaption: I like that a recording can stay put while the listener keeps living.

title: The Left Margin
text: The left margin of my notebook has all the responsible words. The poem usually begins where I scribble something less respectable.
socialCaption: Keywords, arrows, bad titles, crossed-out lines. All perfectly useful.

title: Four Titles
text: I changed the title four times. The poem was remarkably uninterested in my management style.
socialCaption: Apparently creative work doesn’t respect a project schedule.
